info.title: raptor-knee-arms-x
info.subtitle: Single CoAtNet 384 knee MRI arm, 0.917 on the public leaderboard
info.description:
![Dread Development — Johnathan Wagner](https://bojackdidit.github.io/dread-cinematic-banner/dread-orbit-web.webp)

[![Kaggle](https://bojackdidit.github.io/dread-cinematic-banner/buttons/kaggle-bar.png)](https://www.kaggle.com/dreaddevelopment) [![GitHub](https://bojackdidit.github.io/dread-cinematic-banner/buttons/github-bar.png)](https://github.com/Bojackdidit) [![Website](https://bojackdidit.github.io/dread-cinematic-banner/buttons/website-bar.png)](https://dreaddevelopment.com) [![Email](https://bojackdidit.github.io/dread-cinematic-banner/buttons/email-bar.png)](mailto:john@dreaddevelopment.com)

A single CoAtNet 384 arm for the twelve-finding knee MRI task, scoring 0.917 on the public leaderboard.

Trained on all 4,349 labelled studies with 44 slices per study sampled across 15 to 85 percent of each series, a 140 mm crop and 336 pixel images.

This was the shipped model before the slice-sampling work, and it is the baseline every later corpus change is measured against. It also beat a three-backbone ensemble of the previous generation, which is the clearest evidence on this task that corpus quality matters more than model count.

HOW TO USE IT

The checkpoint is a PyTorch dict, not a bare state dict, saved with torch.save. Keys: model (the
weights), arch (the timm backbone name), res (the input size the model expects) and lab (the twelve
finding names in the order the model outputs them). Load it with
torch.load(path, map_location='cpu', weights_only=False), build the backbone from ck['arch'],
attach the twelve-way attention pooling head, then load ck['model'].

A working end-to-end inference notebook, including the preprocessing these weights expect, is here:
https://www.kaggle.com/code/dreaddevelopment/knee-mri-twelve-findings-from-a-single-model

WHAT THE MODEL DOES

Three neighbouring slices are stacked into the three channels of one image, so the network sees a
little of what lies above and below the middle slice. Each of these three-slice windows goes through
the backbone, and the windows are pooled by an attention layer with separate weights for each of the
twelve findings, so each finding can draw on the slices that actually show it.

The twelve findings are ACL tear, MCL tear, medial and lateral meniscus tears, osteoarthritis in the
medial, lateral and patellofemoral compartments, joint effusion, synovitis, a Baker's cyst, bone
contusion and fracture.
